hints: Notice this is the classic iodoform test, so think about what structural feature in W allows a yellow precipitate to form.
Remember the yellow solid in the test with alkaline iodine is always triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$.
Work backwards from the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ fragment to rebuild W by adding back the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ part that was lost as the precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the iodoform reaction**

This is the triiodomethane test. A methyl ketone, $\text{RCOCH}_3$, reacts with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ to give a yellow precipitate.

General equation:
$$\text{RCOCH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Identify the yellow precipitate**

The unmistakable pale yellow precipitate is triiodomethane (iodoform), $\text{CHI}_3$. It is not $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ which is a colourless liquid.

So identity of precipitate:
$$\text{yellow solid} = \text{CHI}_3$$

**Use the carboxylate to find W**

The $\text{CH}_3$ part of $\text{RCOCH}_3$ is cut off to make $\text{CHI}_3$. What is left, $\text{RCO}$, becomes the carboxylate $\text{RCO}_2^-$.

Here $\text{RCO}_2^- = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$, so $\text{R} = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$.

Rebuild W:
$$\text{W} = \text{RCOCH}_3 = \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$$

**Name W**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$ has 4 carbons with the ketone on carbon 2. That is butanone.

This matches butanone plus $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate.

options.A: Correct. Butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$, contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}$ group needed for a positive iodoform test. It gives $\text{CHI}_3$ yellow precipitate and leaves $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$ as the other product.
options.B: W is correct but the precipitate is wrong. $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ (iodomethane) is not formed here and is not a yellow solid. Students sometimes confuse the methyl group with the triiodo product, but all three H atoms on the methyl are replaced by iodine to give $\text{CHI}_3$.
options.C: Precipitate is correct but W is wrong. Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, would also give $\text{CHI}_3$, but its R group is $\text{CH}_3$, so it would give ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-$, not propanoate $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2^-$.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. Propanone would give ethanoate, not the observed propanoate, and $\text{CH}_3\text{I}$ is never the yellow precipitate in this test. This choice confuses both the starting ketone and the iodoform product.
